provenance.note: Standard MIDI Control Change assignments (MIDI spec) — universal CC layer, no device SysEx.

parameters.name: Panpot
parameters.note: p12's received list prints "c = 10 EXPRESSION" and never mentions Pan as a CC, while p19's chart recognises 5,10,11,65 and p13's Reset All Controllers names "PAN 64 (No effect)". Modelled per the MIDI standard (10 Pan, 11 Expression); the Data List is self-contradictory here.

parameters.name: Variation Param 1

parameters.name: Arp/Step Seq Keyboard Mode
parameters.note: p14 common 53h. With Step Seq selected the same byte takes a second, four-member list (*5): normal(0), note-shift&normal(1), ptn-sel&normal(2), ptn-sel&note-shift(3).

parameters.name: Arp/Step Seq Scene Switch (Scene1/Scene2/both)

parameters.name: LFO1 Delay
parameters.note: p14 scene 0Ch. The parameter table misprints this row as a second "LFO1 Speed"; p10's Control Matrix List and Free EG Track Parameter List both enumerate LFO1 Delay as a distinct scene parameter between LFO1 Speed and LFO2 Speed, and 0Ch is the only address left for it. The profile's previous "(sync)" reading is supported by nothing.

parameters.name: VCO1 Wave (type-dependent set)
parameters.note: p14 scene 17h has two lists: with Oscillator Sync off (*4) saw/pulse/saw2/mix (0..3), with it on (*5) saw/pulse/inner1/inner2/inner3 (0..4). Wire 4 is legal only with sync on.

parameters.name: VCO2 Wave
parameters.note: p14 scene 20h: saw(0),pulse(1),saw2(2),mix(3). Unlike VCO1 Wave this has no sync-dependent second list.

parameters.name: Variation Dry:Wet (D63>W..D<W63)
parameters.note: Data List p6, the Wet:Dry column of the Effect Type List. For most types this is a blend, D63>W ... D=W ... D<W63 over 1-127. For Aural Exc and Comp it is a two-way switch — 1-63 reads as dry(1) and 64-127 as wet(127). For Distortion, Over Drive and Amp Sim. it is three-way — dry(1), both(64), wet(127). The Data List footnote *3 also notes the Control Matrix has no effect on VarEF D:W for those five types.

fegTrack.label: Track
fegTrack.note: Free EG recorded curve, four tracks of 192 two-byte points (Data List p14). Track 1 begins at 10 00 68 and each track occupies 384 bytes, so track 2 begins at 10 03 68, track 3 at 10 06 68 and track 4 at 10 09 68. The Data List labels the last point of tracks 3 and 4 "Data128", but the addresses it prints and its own 668h total for the Common block both give every track 192 points.

sceneCtrl.label: Scene Ctrl
sceneCtrl.note: Scene Ctrl buffer (Data List p15: the scene table is addressed 10 1S 00 with S=2 for this buffer, total size 44h). It is the scene block without the control matrix, and the Data List marks it "effective only when Scene Ctrl is active".

parameters.name: Portamento Mode (full-time/fingered)
parameters.note: p14 scene 06h has two label sets: with Poly Mode = poly (*1) normal(0)/sustain-key(1); with Poly Mode = mono or legato (*2) full-time(0)/fingered(1).

parameters.name: LFO1 Delay
parameters.note: p14 scene 0Ch. The parameter table misprints this row as a second "LFO1 Speed"; p10's Control Matrix List and Free EG Track Parameter List both enumerate LFO1 Delay as a distinct scene parameter between LFO1 Speed and LFO2 Speed, and 0Ch is the only address left for it. The profile's previous "(sync)" reading is supported by nothing.

parameters.name: VCO1 Wave (type-dependent set)
parameters.note: p14 scene 17h has two lists: with Oscillator Sync off (*4) saw/pulse/saw2/mix (0..3), with it on (*5) saw/pulse/inner1/inner2/inner3 (0..4). Wire 4 is legal only with sync on.

parameters.name: VCO2 Wave
parameters.note: p14 scene 20h: saw(0),pulse(1),saw2(2),mix(3). Unlike VCO1 Wave this has no sync-dependent second list.

parameters.name: Reserved (43h)
parameters.note: Reserved. The Data List gives this byte the single value 00; it is here so the block maps end to end.

dumps.name: Current Voice Common
dumps.note: Data List p14, MIDI Data Table <1-3>: TOTAL SIZE 668h = 1640 bytes — 104 bytes of named parameters followed by the four Free EG curve tracks.

dumps.name: User Voice (bank)
dumps.note: Bulk dump only (Data List p15, MIDI Data Table <1-6>): 796h = 1942 bytes, laid out as Voice Common, Scene 1, Scene 2, Step Seq. mm = 00...7F selects User Voice 1...128, so the address byte is the $slot variable. The Free EG curve region (offsets 104...1639) is deliberately unmapped — a captured voice is replayed byte for byte.

dumps.name: User Step SEQ Pattern (bank)
dumps.note: Bulk dump only (Data List p17/p18, MIDI Data Table <1-7>): 46h = 70 bytes with the Current Step SEQ layout. mm = 00...7F selects User Pattern 1...128.

provenance.note: Transcribed from the official Yamaha AN1x Data List (MIDI Data Format). CC: full MODE2 per-parameter Control Change map (set the AN1x MIDI Control Mode to 2). SysEx parameter change F0 43 1n 5C addr3 data F7 (model 5C, no checksum): System block (00 00 00, complete), Voice Common (10 00 00: name in dump, effects/EQ/arp/free-EG config), Voice Scene 1/2 (10 10 00 / 10 11 00, full synth voice + 16-slot control matrix). Bulk dump F0 43 0n 5C bcMSB bcLSB addr3 data cs F7 with a negated 7-bit checksum (roland-7bit in this codebase; p13: the sum of byte count, address, data and the checksum itself is 0 mod 128); request F0 43 2n 5C addr3 F7. Full dump receive layouts verified for System and Scene buffers; Voice Common / Scene Ctrl / Step SEQ / User banks are request-only (their bulk-dump-only arrays, e.g. per-step Free EG data, are not transcribed). Presets: the Data List's MIDI Implementation Chart marks Bank Select (CC 0 / CC 32) as neither transmitted nor recognized, so voices are selected by Program Change alone (0...127, transmitted and recognized). The 128 factory voice names are the Data List's Factory-set Voice List. The 128 User voices are addressable only by bulk dump (11 00 00...11 7F 00) and have no Program Change of their own, so they are not modelled as a bank: PRESET/USER is a front-panel choice the AN1x does not expose over MIDI. Device number: the AN1x puts it in the LOW nibble of byte 3 and the high nibble is the substatus — 1n parameter change, 0n bulk dump, 2n dump request. The profile writes 10 / 00 / 20, i.e. n=0 (device number 1), which is what the instrument answers at its factory setting (System 0Ah defaults to "all"). A non-default device number needs those three bytes changed together; the engine has no way to compute them from one variable.
